cultural.vision_reason: The picture shows a handmade Hausa horse forehead ornament or trapping, made from decorated leather, cloth, and metal elements. It fits Hausa material culture, though it is an animal adornment rather than a garment.

physical.title: horse-trappings
physical.summary:
Horse forehead ornament composed of three elements: decorated strip, two semi-spherical ornaments and a flat leather connecting bar. The forehead decoration is in form of three interconnecting bars made of leather covered with alternating green and yellow cotton cloth. Further ornamented with tin (gold and silver effect) strips pushed through the leather or glued to additional curved pieces of leather whose tips are pushed through the leather bars. Semi-spherical ornaments are decorated with blue, green and yellow cotton cloth, pink synthetic cloth and central black wool ? cloth with cut out decoration revealing red cotton cloth and metal staples. Connecting red-dyed leather bar has dot decoration in black ink and synthetic red and blue cloth covering on back.
Plaited leather straps attached to semi-spheres.
